clue.text: The language of Hamlet — old lines providing quite a mouthful

parts.note: Hamlet was Prince of Denmark, so his tongue is Danish
old means past, gone by
RY is the abbreviation for railway, the lines a train runs on

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare buff marvels that Hamlet's archaic verse is a lot to get one's tongue round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite a mouthful' looks like a comment on the verse, but it is the definition: a pastry is a big bite.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sweet breakfast bun is a substantial bite to eat, playfully called a mouthful.

clue.text: Sole cleaner is a feeble person

definitions.meaning: a mat for wiping the soles of shoes
a weak person others walk all over

explanation.surface: A shoe-cleaning mat is compared to a spineless individual.
explanation.definitionFit: A mat by the entrance for wiping shoes, and a submissive person who gets trampled on, share this name.

clue.text: One likely to succeed, though illegitimate

definitions.meaning: an old term for a child born outside marriage

explanation.surface: Someone talented is destined for success despite being born out of wedlock.
explanation.definitionFit: A gifted person born to excel, and an archaic word for born out of wedlock, share this word.

clue.text: Refused it, being poorly and too full

indicators.note: poorly suggests the letters are in a bad way and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone refused food because they felt ill and already overfull.
explanation.definitionFit: Overfed past the point of satisfaction, glutted.

clue.text: Make a fuss over appeal that's legally insignificant

parts.note: to pet is to fondle or make a fuss over
it is slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Someone fusses over a legal appeal of small importance.
explanation.definitionFit: Law French for small or minor, as in petty larceny.

clue.text: Go to live outside a city in America

indicators.note: outside means the word for going to live goes around the following letter

parts.note: to settle is to go and make a home somewhere

explanation.surface: Someone moves to live outside a US city.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pacific Northwest port in Washington State is a large city of the USA.

clue.text: State letters that have point will get swift reply

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
the post means letters delivered
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Official letters with a pointed message prompt a quick retort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that have' and 'will get' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick sharp retort, originally a fencer's return thrust.

clue.text: He's in charge of flats and other properties

definitions.text: He's in charge of flats and other properties

parts.words: He's in charge of flats and other properties
parts.note: flats are pieces of theatre scenery and properties are props, so this is the person running the backstage

explanation.surface: A man manages a portfolio of apartments and other real estate.
explanation.definitionFit: The person running the stage during a theatre production oversees scenery and props.

clue.text: Start to fall, catching right foot

indicators.note: catching means the wobbling word holds the other letter inside it

parts.note: to totter is to sway as if about to fall

explanation.surface: Someone begins to topple and grabs a right foot to steady themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A pig's foot, eaten as food, is called by this name.

clue.text: Go back to capture pawn that's unable to escape

indicators.note: to capture means the reversed word takes the other letter inside it
back here tells us to read the word for go from right to left

parts.note: to go is to depart
P is the chess abbreviation for pawn

explanation.surface: A chess player retreats a piece to take a pawn that cannot get away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DEPART into TRAPED, and 'to capture' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something caught in a snare is held fast with no way out.

clue.text: Criticising for being too casually got up

definitions.meaning: dressed down, in clothes too informal

explanation.surface: Someone is being reprimanded for turning up underdressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe reprimand, and wearing deliberately informal clothes, share this phrase.

clue.text: Suitable arboreal habitat for stick insect?

definitions.text: Suitable arboreal habitat for stick insect?

parts.words: Suitable arboreal habitat for stick insect?
parts.note: read 'stick' as glue: an insect that sticks would suit a tree that oozes sticky resin, the eucalyptus

explanation.surface: A naturalist wonders which tree a stick insect would best live in.
explanation.definitionFit: The eucalyptus is commonly named for the sticky resin it exudes, which would suit something clinging.

clue.text: Drink teas blended as one prefers

parts.note: a tot is a small drink of spirits

indicators.note: blended means the letters of the following word are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone mixes a drink from blended teas to suit their own preference.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe seasoned according to personal liking is seasoned this way.

clue.text: Gold, say, was in contact with aluminium

parts.note: met means came into contact with
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A gold item was touching some aluminium.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold is one example of an element of this class; 'say' flags the example.

clue.text: Teachers dropping out each quarter before head makes short speech

indicators.note: before means the compass letter comes ahead of the headland word
dropping out means the letters of the next word are taken out of the first word

parts.note: E, for east, is one quarter of the compass
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: Teachers quitting one by one before the head gives a brief address.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing E, A, C, H from TEACHERS leaves TERS. 'makes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Brevity of expression, saying little in few words, is a curt manner of speaking.

clue.text: Presses on, getting curious answers

indicators.note: curious, meaning odd, tells us the letters are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone presses on despite getting strange answers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curious' rearranges PRESSES ON; 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Replies given to questions are another word for this.

clue.text: Small movement of sea, despite an explosion

indicators.note: an explosion blows the letters of the preceding words apart into a new order

explanation.surface: The sea stirs only slightly despite a blast nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest range between high and low water comes at certain lunar phases.

clue.text: Upper classes meeting dishonour and decline

parts.note: A and B are the top social grades in UK market research
a stain is a mark of disgrace

explanation.surface: Upper classes meet with disgrace and fall into decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decline' looks like a noun, but it is a verb: to refuse, to hold back from voting.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain or refuse to take part, as when not voting.

clue.text: Sign Handel originally entered over a passage for wind

indicators.note: entered means the initial letter goes into the word for sign

parts.note: a trace is a sign or mark left behind

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A sign of Handel entered over a passage for wind instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a link. The wind is breath, not music.
explanation.definitionFit: The windpipe carries air, or breath, between throat and lungs.

clue.text: Boy behind mother who wears apron?

indicators.note: behind means the word for boy comes after the word for mother

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a son is a boy child

explanation.surface: A boy trails behind his mother, who is wearing a pinafore.
explanation.walkthrough: The apron is not a kitchen one: Freemasons wear ceremonial aprons, as stonemasons wore working ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonemasons and Freemasons both wear an apron as part of their dress.

clue.text: Agencies overlooking note to broker

indicators.note: overlooking means the word for agencies sits on top, coming first in this down clue

parts.note: the media are agencies of communication
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Agencies look past a note to a stockbroker.
explanation.definitionFit: To act as go-between and arrange a deal between two parties.

clue.text: A colour for Hester Prynne

parts.note: Hester Prynne is the heroine of Hawthorne's novel in which she must wear an adulterer's red letter A

explanation.surface: Someone picks a colour for a literary heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: The bright red of the letter in Hawthorne's novel is this shade.

clue.text: Finally buying land to develop

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word that follows

parts.note: an estate is a tract of land

explanation.surface: In the end a buyer acquires land to build on.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry young in the womb is to let them grow there.

clue.text: Went carefully, promised no place at the outset

indicators.note: no here means the abbreviation for place is taken away from the word for promised
at the outset says the removed letters come from the very start of the word

parts.note: pledged means promised

explanation.surface: Someone moved cautiously, having been guaranteed no starting position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no ... at the outset' removes PL from the front of PLEDGED.
explanation.definitionFit: To move slowly and cautiously, inch by inch, sideways along something.

clue.text: Unwanted card one's left on shelf

definitions.meaning: the card game in which the queen left unpaired loses
a woman supposedly left unmarried, an old-fashioned term

explanation.surface: Someone describes an unwanted card that ends up left on a shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a children's card game with an unwanted card and an outdated term for a spinster go by this name.

clue.text: He won't let people go round his estate, perhaps

definitions.text: He won't let people go round his estate, perhaps

parts.words: He won't let people go round his estate, perhaps
parts.note: the estate is an estate car, and the man won't let other drivers overtake it

explanation.surface: A landowner refuses visitors permission to walk around his grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A selfish driver who blocks others from passing is the target of this insult.

clue.text: Meekly accept this is no guarantee summer's here

definitions.meaning: to put up with something without protest

definitions.text: this is no guarantee summer's here
definitions.meaning: the proverb says one migrating bird of this kind does not make a summer

explanation.surface: Someone resignedly accepts that a single sign is no promise of warm weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Accepting an insult without objection, and a migrant bird from the proverb, share this word.

clue.text: Very bright, of American parentage

parts.note: the Inca were native South Americans, so Incan is a kind of American
descent means ancestry or parentage

explanation.surface: Someone is described as brilliant and born to American parents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American' suggests the USA, but here it is South American: of Incan descent. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowing white with heat, a lamp filament shines brilliantly.
